summary: Overall quality is high. All numeric keys were recomputed and are correct (Pearl index 2, cumulative risk 24.6%, TMSC 28.8, RMI 450 and 3,060, PPV 19.6%, MMR 73.1, shock index 1.28, twin discordance 25%, BMI 16.4, fibroid volume 73.3, fold change 8, true positives 114, progesterone day 25, MMR fall 39.5%). Drug regimens checked against my recollection of current guidance were consistent: BASHH ceftriaxone 1 g IM, doxycycline 100 mg bd for 7 days, benzathine benzylpenicillin 2.4 MU, ulipristal 30 mg, levonorgestrel 1.5 mg or 3 mg, betamethasone 12 mg x2, magnesium sulfate 4 g then 1 g/h, UKMEC categories, PPROM erythromycin, Quintero staging and RMI scoring. The main problems are a FIGO 2018 size-boundary error for stage IB, a marking guide that presents GnRH analogues as contraceptive, and several omissions in safety-relevant caveats (ulipristal and hormonal contraception interval, doxycycline in pregnancy). No literal \uXXXX escapes, '[object Object]' or garbled characters were found. Confidence is moderate to high, but this is an AI review: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (clinician) before clinical reliance, and all regimens and thresholds should be checked against current FSRH, BASHH, NICE and RCOG sources.

issues.problem: FIGO 2018 stage IB size boundaries are misstated: 'IB1 under 2 cm, IB2 2 cm to under 4 cm' and 'IB3 ... 4 cm or more' (table and worked example). FIGO 2018 defines IB1 as 2 cm or less, IB2 as more than 2 cm up to and including 4 cm, and IB3 as more than 4 cm. A 4.0 cm tumour would be mis-staged as IB3 (chemoradiation) rather than IB2 (surgery). Keys for the 2.6 cm (IB2) and 5 cm (IB3) examples are unaffected.
issues.suggestedFix: Restate as IB1 up to and including 2 cm, IB2 more than 2 cm up to and including 4 cm, IB3 more than 4 cm (and IIA1 up to 4 cm, IIA2 more than 4 cm), in the table, the worked-example step and the q006 explanation. Source check against the FIGO 2018 staging paper.

issues.problem: Marking guide: 'Hormonal suppression (combined pill, progestogens, GnRH analogues) works by preventing ovulation and so is contraceptive'. GnRH analogues are not reliable contraception (women are advised to use non-hormonal contraception during treatment and they must not be used in pregnancy); some progestogens used for endometriosis (for example dydrogesterone) also do not reliably inhibit ovulation. A student could wrongly rely on a GnRH analogue as contraception.
issues.suggestedFix: State that combined hormonal contraception, desogestrel or other ovulation-inhibiting progestogens and the LNG-IUS also give contraception, but GnRH analogues and some progestogens do not, so barrier or other non-hormonal contraception is needed; all suppressive treatments are stopped to conceive.

issues.problem: Ulipristal worked example plans 'ongoing contraception' without the FSRH interaction advice. Ulipristal antagonises progestogens, so starting or resuming hormonal contraception must wait 5 days after ulipristal (condoms or abstinence meanwhile, with a further 7 days, or 9 for the oestradiol valerate/dienogest pill, before contraceptive cover). The lesson also does not state that levonorgestrel can be followed immediately by hormonal contraception.
issues.suggestedFix: Add that after ulipristal, hormonal contraception should be started no sooner than 5 days later with extra precautions, and that a Cu-IUD avoids this issue. Source check against current FSRH emergency contraception guidance.

issues.problem: Lesson classes DMPA as LARC and says LARC has 'typical-use failure close to perfect-use failure', but its own table gives DMPA typical-use failure of about 6%. The summary 'LARC has the lowest typical-use failure' is also not true for DMPA.
issues.suggestedFix: Qualify the statement to the implant, LNG-IUS and Cu-IUD (below 1%), noting DMPA depends on timely repeat injections every 13 weeks.

issues.problem: Abortion law is described as the Abortion Act 1967 with two-doctor certification and Ground C, and q008 asserts this as current for England and Wales. Recent UK legislation concerning decriminalisation of a woman's own abortion in England and Wales may have changed the criminal-law framing; I cannot verify its current status. Home use of early medical abortion up to 9 weeks 6 days is also not mentioned.
issues.suggestedFix: Source check the current legal position and add a note on the current lawful framework and telemedical early medical abortion pathway; keep the two-doctor and 24-week content only if still accurate.

issues.problem: Chlamydia treatment is given as 'Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (azithromycin if doxycycline unsuitable)' with no mention that doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy, even though the lesson discusses chlamydia in pregnancy.
issues.suggestedFix: Add that doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy and azithromycin (or alternatives per BASHH) is used, with test of cure in pregnancy.

issues.problem: PID regimen: 'intramuscular ceftriaxone plus doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days' is ambiguous: ceftriaxone (1 g IM) is a single dose, while doxycycline and metronidazole are given for 14 days, and no doses are given. It could be read as 14 days of IM ceftriaxone.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose plus doxycycline 100 mg bd and metronidazole 400 mg bd for 14 days (teaching example; check current BASHH).

issues.problem: Tranexamic acid is listed under haemorrhage 'prevention' (lesson prevention paragraph and marking guide 'Haemorrhage prevention: ... tranexamic acid'). Evidence (WOMAN trial) supports tranexamic acid as treatment of established PPH, given within 3 hours; routine prophylactic use at every birth is not standard.
issues.suggestedFix: Move tranexamic acid to PPH treatment (1 g IV within 3 hours of birth); keep oxytocin-based active management of the third stage as the prevention measure.

issues.problem: For a UK clinical-year course the unit is framed mainly around low-resource settings (three delays, home birth 60 km away) while the UK obstetric collapse content is thin: no left lateral tilt versus manual displacement distinction for non-arrest collapse, no local anaesthetic toxicity (lipid emulsion) or magnesium overdose dosing detail, and the resuscitative hysterotomy statement gives no UK source (RCUK/RCOG). Objectives are otherwise covered. Subject metadata also labels the course Year5 while it was commissioned as clinical Year 4.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a short UK maternal collapse algorithm (recognition, call for help, left lateral tilt or manual uterine displacement, resuscitative hysterotomy by 5 minutes, causes 4Hs/4Ts including local anaesthetic toxicity and magnesium toxicity) and confirm the intended year label.

issues.problem: Screening recall intervals are deferred ('intervals have been revised ... check current policy') and CIN management after treatment (test of cure timing) is only mentioned in passing, although the unit objectives include describing how screening and colposcopy detect precancer.
issues.suggestedFix: State the current NHS England recall intervals for hrHPV-negative women (recently extended for ages 25 to 49; source check required) and give test-of-cure timing after LLETZ (hrHPV test at about 6 months).
